cells.remarks: Gives a list of endowments in land and money made by Mallaiya-Daṇṇayaka for the deity Gōkarṇa, and for the Baidhe for offerings to the deity, for burning a lamp in front of the image of Brahmidēva and for feeding pil-grims during the time of Dēvappa-Daṇṇayaka.

cells.location: SOUTH KANARA DISTRICT / COONDAPOOR TALUK · Bainduru † — Karnataka
cells.place: On the slab of Sankesvara †
cells.date:
Śaka 1371, Śōkla, Chaitra, su. 10, Thursday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 537: Śaka 1371, Sukla, Chaitra, śu. 10, Thursday.
Probably A.D. 1449, April 17, Thursday. Śu. 10 is probably a mistake for ba. 10]
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land for offerings and worship in the basti of Pārasvanātha, while Indagaṇṇa-Oḍeya, son of Saṅgi-rāya-Oḍeya, was governing the Haḍuvalli-rājya.

cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to record endowment of land by purchase, to the temple of Sayanēśvara at Bayndūru by Chikka Malaiya-Daṇṇayaka, the younger brother of Mahā-pradhāna Malaiya-Daṇṇayaka, the governor of Baṅkaru-rājya.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the outer grakdra of Sayanēsvara temple. †
cells.date: Saka 1446, Chitra-bhanu, Magha, su. 5 and Saka 1446, Svabhanu.
cells.remarks: Records that, while Mahamandalesvara Devarasa-Odeya, governor of Sangitapura, was governing Baiduru and other divisions from his capital Sangitapura, Sankana-Sombara, son of Narana Sombara, made a gift of land to the temple of Samesvaradeva for offerings and for the maintenance of a feeding-house as well as for the worship of the god Gopinatha installed in it. Mentions Bindupuri (Bainduru).

cells.location: SOUTH KANARA DISTRICT / COONDAPOOR TALUK · Bainduru † — Karnataka
cells.place: On a slab into the compound wall of a private house near Sayanēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that, while Mahamandalesvara Channa-Setti-devi-Amma, a ruling queen, was governing the districts from Sangitapura, an endowment of land was made by Charabaiya-Setti for worship in the daily six Brah-mans in a matha built by him, while Basavara-Odeya was governing Barakuru-rajya. Before the rule of Indigarasa-Odeya, son of Mahamandalesvara Sangitapura-rajya-governor, was also mentioned.

cells.place: On a slab lying by the side of the tank called 'Hoakere' near Sayanēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Mentions Charabaiya-Setti-Amma, daughter of Bayira-devi-Amma, as ruling over Baiduru and other places from Sangitapura. Records endowment, after purchase, of two plots of land to the Kosavasvara-Setti to the [matha] built by him.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers grant of land by eight partners of Bayiduru-nadu while governing women, to Vidyanatha-devarajaiya, while [Baramara-O]deya was governing the Barakuru-rajya.

cells.remarks: Mentions Atyappa-Oḍeya as administering the kingdom under the orders of the king. The temple is said to have been built by Śaṅku-Heggade, the aḷiya of Hosabanna-Seṭṭi, of the family of Maṭhu-Seṭṭi of Koḷekēri.

Kaṇharadeva.
Śaka 117[8], Nala, Pushya, ba. 30, Monday, solar eclipse, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkramaṇa.
The details are not correct for Nala, in which year there was no solar eclipse on Pushya, ba. 30, nor did this tithi fall on Monday. But in the previous year, i.e., Rākshasa, there was a solar eclipse on Pushya, ba. 30, but this fell on Sunday and did not coincide with the Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkranti of the year. By the coincidence of the eclipse and the tithi, the intended date might correspond to A.D. 1255, January 10, Sunday. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 32]

8th year, Jivana, Pushya, su. 10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 74: 8th year, Īśvara, Pushya, śu. 10, Monday Īśvara would be the 8th year for three kings, viz., (1) the Western Chālukya king Trailōkyamalla (Nūrmadi-Taila III), (2) the Yādava king Siṅghaṇa (according to Fleet) and (3) the Yādava king Rāmachandra. In Īśvara, falling in Nūrmadi-Taila's reign, Pausha, śu. 10 fell on a Friday; in Siṅghaṇa's reign, the tithi fell on Saturday; and in Rāmachandra's reign, it fell on Tuesday.
But in Siṅghaṇa's reign in Īśvara, Pausha, ba. 10 fell on a Monday. Assuming that śu. 10 is a mistake for ba. 10, the record might be assigned to his reign and the date would correspond to A.D. 1217, December 25, Monday. The characters do not militate against this assignment.]

cells.location: BIJAPUR DISTRICT / MUDDEBIHAL TALUK · Muttingi † — Karnataka
cells.place: the slab of Siddharāmayya †
cells.date: Pārthiva, Āshādha, ba. 10, Thursday, Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 110: Pārthiva, Āshāḍha, ba. 10, Thursday, Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti. Considering the sequence of the inscription on the slab, Parthiva might be taken to be the first Pārthiva coming after A.D. 1142. But the tithi on the day of Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti was not Āshāḍha, ba. 10, but it was śu. 5; and the saṁkrānti commenced only on the following Friday. But in the next Pārthiva (i.e., A.D. 1225), the Dakshināyana-saṁkrānti actually began on Thursday, June 26. This might be the corresponding English date though the tithi was not Āshāḍha, ba. 10, but ba. 5.]

Mentions the Mahājñas of the Brahmapuri of the god and the araṇi-guttiga (tenant) of the garden, Bammaṇa, who was to supply the flower-garlands and vegetables required for the temple. The settiguttas and nakharas of Muttage contributed bdellium, etc., required for the festivals of the deity, while the Mahājñas granted one oil-mill together with the site on which it stood.

Śaka 1174, Virōdhakrit, Śrāvaṇa, śu. paurnami, Sunday, eclipse, saṅkrānti, Vyati pāta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 114: Śaka 1174, Virōdhikṛit, Śrāvaṇa, śu. paurṇamī, Sunday, eclipse, saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta.
In Virōdhikṛit, Śrāvaṇa, there was no eclipse ou paurṇamī nor did this paurṇamī fall on Sunday; but on Āśvina-paurṇamī of this year which fell on Sunday there was the only lunar eclipse of the year. But the saṅkrānti (i.e., Tulā-saṅkrānti) had occurred three days previously (i.e., Friday). Śrāvaṇa is probably cited wrongly for Āśvina. The date would correspond to A.D. 1251, October 1, Sunday.]
cells.remarks: Records the gifts of lands, oil, etc., made by Siripayya, the son of Hariyanna of Hagaraṭtage, who belonged to the Va[ji]-vaṅśa and was the Śrikaraṇa of the Mahāpradhaṇa Rāyadaṇdādhiśa Saredādhikari, Chaudi-Setti who was governing over the Two [Be]? valas, Banavasi-Pandyanaṇu, Hanum[gal-Pandinādu], Tardavaḍi, etc., countries while the latter's maternal uncle Kaṅgarasa was governing the villages of Salavādige, Bagavadi, etc. The gift was made for the benefit of the temple of Gōpaladēva and of the sixteen Mahājñas attached to the deity. Records also gifts of lands made to the temples of Lakshmaṇēsvaradēva and Bhaskaradēva.

cells.language: Kannada (verse) †
cells.remarks: This is a composite record registering several facts and gifts. Prases king Subhātungavallabha born in the Rāshtrakūta-kula and mentions Krishna II and Kanhavallabha who are respectively the name and surname of Krishna II, who is also called Krishnarāja in the inscription. States that his subordinate Hirayamma-Sangata built a temple and made provisions for worship and offerings and some land to it. Subsequently, when this temple fell into ruin a Sūyavatisāmand Mōrudevimani renovated it and consecrated in it the two deities of Siddheśvara and Śiva. Some time later the king's feudatory Gundayya, son of King Jagadeamalla of the Chalukya line descended from King Nūrmadi Tailapa, by Chikabbe, the daughter of four curtain Mahāga Makamayya. Gifts made by the four curtain mahājanas of the palace, the gaudas, the setties, the Airanyanīru and Vaji-vardhana, by the residents of the village and the Three-Hundred Vajjani/ligas are also recorded.
